text:
alice: Heads-up: after today's canary we saw p95 token latency increase on long-context workloads. Digging in — looks tied to the KV layer pager thrash when continuous batching merges grow large.
ben: Repro steps? any flame graphs/heap profiles?
alice: Yes, attaching quick notes: page-in/page-out spikes during merged requests; KV reuse for sessions >32k tokens drops from ~92% to ~63%. Flame link: https://perf/reports/1937 (private)
carla: That smells like head-of-line blocking: when a merged batch serializes page IO for the lead request, subsequent merged requests wait. Merge window + merge size may be trading latency for batch efficiency.
dmitri: Merge window currently at 35ms in canary. If a slow page read happens it drags the whole merged proto. We also see fragment count increasing (more small allocations) which worsens eviction churn.
alice: Repro harness command: 
```bash
# contbatch stress: reproducer
./harness --mode=contbatch --clients=120 --seqlen=4096 --overlap=0.4 --duration=3m
```
ben: Logs show repeated "kv_pager: fetch_pages start/end" pairs for same session separated by evictions. Looks like reuse broken by evict-read-reuse race.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: metric kv_cache_hit_rate dropped 29% at 2026-03-17T14:03Z; kv_evictions/sec up 4.5x.
carla: Short-term mitigations proposal: 1) cap merge window to 8ms; 2) only merge requests from same session or same affinity token; 3) increase pager prefetch concurrency to avoid serial blocking.
dmitri: Long-term: per-shard LRU with age buckets and a background async pager that does read-ahead and doesn't block the main request path. Also consider max_merge_tokens to avoid mega-merges for long contexts.
alice: Agree. Can we ship the merge cap + same-session-only merge as a low-risk canary? That should reduce head-of-line locks at the cost of some batching.
ben: +1. Add metrics before shipping: merged_batch_size, merge_wait_ms, pages_fetched_per_merge, kv_reuse_rate_by_session_len.
carla: Also add a runtime flag: runtime.kv.merge_mode=prefer_session so it's easy to toggle.
admitri: (typo) dmitri: FYI if we cap too aggressively throughput (tokens/sec) could regress; need to run throughput harness to quantify.
alice: I'll open a small PR that adds the flags + telemetry and a perf test. Will canary to 10% traffic.
ben: If eviction thrash persists after merge changes, we should experiment with shard sizing and keeping a small working set hotter (pin recent prefixes).
carla: Note: we also observed the regression impacting function-calling flows where token counts are small but concurrency is high — merge heuristics should treat those differently.
alice: Thanks — will post heap profiles and the flamegraph in the PR. @oncall-sre please watch p95/p99 and kv_evictions after deploy.
oncall-sre: noted, will alert on kv_evictions > 200/s or p95 token latency increase > 15%.
carla: One more thought: add a fast-path for "no-page-miss" merges: if all requests' KV fingerprints indicate hot residency, allow larger merges. Low risk and keeps batching benefits.
dmitri: Good idea. We can add a quick residency precheck (cheap bitmap) before merging.
alice: Cool. I'll include that as an opt-in in the PR. Posting follow-up numbers after the throughput run. :rocket:
